draftA:
REQ-1: The readiness gate applies only to CO-50 medical-necessity denials; denials of any other class are unaffected by it.
REQ-2: On a CO-50 denial, "Mark appeal packet ready" is blocked unless both are present: a non-empty clinical-note reference in DOC-### form, and a filing-deadline date.
REQ-3: The filing deadline is date of service plus 90 days (Northwind Health timely filing); the system computes it from DOS and stores it as the deadline field.
REQ-4: No role may override the gate in v1; when blocked, the button label names exactly which of the two items is missing.
AC-1: CO-50, DOS 2024-03-01 gives deadline 2024-05-30, note ref DOC-204 present: button is enabled and the packet is marked ready. (Second check: DOS 2025-01-15 gives 2025-04-15.)
AC-2: CO-50 with deadline 2024-05-30 present but note ref blank: action blocked, button reads "Add clinical note reference".
AC-3: CO-50 with DOC-204 present but no deadline: blocked, button reads "Add filing deadline". With both missing: blocked, button reads "Add clinical note reference and filing deadline".
AC-4: A non-CO-50 denial with both fields empty can still be marked ready; a blocked CO-50 stays blocked for every user and role, with no override path.
draftB:
REQ-1: On CO-50 denials only, do not allow the appeal packet to be marked ready unless a non-empty DOC-### clinical-note id and a filing-deadline date are both present, and allow no override in v1.
REQ-2: The filing deadline is the date of service plus 90 days under Northwind Health timely filing.
REQ-3: When blocked, the button names exactly what is missing.
AC-1: CO-50 with DOC-100 and date of service 2025-01-01 has filing deadline 2025-04-01 and may be marked ready.
AC-2: CO-50 with no DOC-### id and date of service 2025-01-01 is blocked, and the button names only the missing clinical-note id.
AC-3: CO-50 with DOC-100 and no date of service is blocked, and the button names only the missing filing deadline.
AC-4: CO-50 missing both items is blocked and the button names both; a non-CO-50 denial missing both is not blocked; nobody can override in v1.

reviewOfA.strengths: The draft correctly limits the gate to CO-50, requires a non-empty DOC-### note id and a DOS-plus-90 deadline with no override, and both acceptance dates check out: 2024-03-01 plus 90 days is 2024-05-30, and 2025-01-15 plus 90 days is 2025-04-15.

findings.title: No test for malformed DOC id
findings.detail: Facts define the clinical-note reference as a non-empty DOC-### id, but acceptance only covers present (DOC-100) versus absent. Nothing verifies that a malformed or whitespace value (for example "DOC-", "ABC-123", or " ") is treated as missing and blocks the packet.
findings.quote: AC-2: CO-50 with no DOC-### id and date of service 2025-01-01 is blocked, and the button names only the missing clinical-note id.

findings.title: AC-4 bundles three separate scenarios
findings.detail: One criterion mixes the both-missing CO-50 case, the non-CO-50 exemption, and the no-override rule. Each needs its own pass/fail test so a partial failure is visible rather than hidden inside a single compound assertion.
findings.quote: AC-4: CO-50 missing both items is blocked and the button names both; a non-CO-50 denial missing both is not blocked; nobody can override in v1.

findings.title: Override ban stated, not testable
findings.detail: "Nobody can override in v1" asserts a rule without a scenario: no actor attempts an override and no expected outcome is defined. Add a case where a specialist (or any role) tries to bypass the gate and the attempt fails.

reviewOfB.strengths: The filing-deadline arithmetic is correct: date of service 2025-01-01 plus 90 days in non-leap 2025 is indeed 2025-04-01, and the CO-50-only scope and no-override rule are carried through faithfully.

merge.document:
REQ-1: The readiness gate applies only to CO-50 medical-necessity denials; denials of any other class are unaffected.
REQ-2: On a CO-50 denial, "Mark appeal packet ready" is blocked unless both are present: a non-empty clinical-note reference in DOC-### form, and a filing-deadline date. A value that is blank, whitespace, or not in DOC-### form counts as missing.
REQ-3: The filing deadline is date of service plus 90 days (Northwind Health timely filing); the system computes it from DOS and stores it as the deadline field.
REQ-4: No role may override the gate in v1; when blocked, the button label names exactly which of the two items is missing.
AC-1: CO-50, DOS 2024-03-01 gives deadline 2024-05-30, note ref DOC-204 present: button is enabled and the packet is marked ready. (Date checks: DOS 2025-01-15 gives 2025-04-15; DOS 2025-01-01 gives 2025-04-01.)
AC-2: CO-50 with deadline 2024-05-30 present but note ref blank: blocked, button reads "Add clinical note reference".
AC-3: CO-50 with deadline present and note ref "DOC-", "ABC-123", or " ": each is treated as missing, blocked, button reads "Add clinical note reference".
AC-4: CO-50 with DOC-204 present but no deadline: blocked, button reads "Add filing deadline".
AC-5: CO-50 with both items missing: blocked, button reads "Add clinical note reference and filing deadline".
AC-6: A non-CO-50 denial with both fields empty can still be marked ready.
AC-7: A specialist, and any other role, attempting to mark a blocked CO-50 packet ready (including by direct action outside the button) is refused; the packet stays not ready and no override path exists.
merge.keptFromA: I kept draft A's four-requirement structure, its explicit DOS-plus-90 computation and storage statement, and its verified example dates (2024-03-01 to 2024-05-30, 2025-01-15 to 2025-04-15) plus the exact blocked-button wording.
merge.keptFromB: I kept draft B's tight CO-50-only phrasing of the gate condition, its correct 2025-01-01 to 2025-04-01 example, and its clean one-case-per-criterion split of the missing-note and missing-deadline scenarios.

resolutions.finding: D-B1 - No test for malformed DOC id
resolutions.note: Added REQ-2 wording that blank, whitespace, or non-DOC-### values count as missing, and AC-3 testing "DOC-", "ABC-123", and " ".

resolutions.finding: D-B2 - AC-4 bundles three separate scenarios
resolutions.note: Split into AC-5 (both missing on CO-50), AC-6 (non-CO-50 exemption), and AC-7 (no override), each independently pass/fail.

resolutions.finding: D-B3 - Override ban stated, not testable
resolutions.note: AC-7 now names an actor (specialist or any role) attempting to bypass the gate and the expected outcome: refused, packet stays not ready.

resolutions.finding: Review of draft A - no defects found
resolutions.note: Dates in draft A check out, but the review missed two gaps: no malformed DOC-### case and no explicit override-attempt scenario; both are covered in AC-3 and AC-7.
